claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially exists in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a composition-dependent thermodynamic instability triggered by differential Al mobility.
At intermediate temperatures, Al tends to segregate because of its size and bonding differences relative to the other constituents.
Al segregation creates local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions lower the free-energy barrier for nucleating ordered secondary phases from the BCC state.
Candidate secondary phases include B2 or sigma phases.
Isothermal aging near 650°C produces Al-enriched clusters or nanoscale precipitates.
Al-enriched clusters or nanoscale precipitates act as nucleation sites for secondary-phase formation.
At intermediate temperatures, Al diffuses faster than the other constituents.
Differential Al diffusion produces local composition fluctuations and Al-rich regions.
Al-rich regions destabilize the overall BCC structure through lattice distortion.
Formation of an ordered secondary phase is thermodynamically favorable at intermediate temperatures.
Competition between the thermodynamic driving force for Al-induced phase separation and kinetic hindrance from limited diffusion explains the phase-stability regimes.
The volume fraction of the secondary ordered phase will progressively increase with aging time at 650°C.
Secondary-phase formation will produce new X-ray diffraction peaks and Al-enriched regions detectable by TEM/EDS.
Rapid quenching from the high-temperature BCC state retains a single-phase microstructure without significant diffusion-driven segregation.
The proposed mechanism operates around 600–700°C because Al diffusion is active in that range.
At significantly lower temperatures, diffusion is too sluggish to permit phase separation.
At higher temperatures, increased solubility may maintain the homogeneous BCC structure.
Failure to detect secondary phases, Al-enriched clusters, or other microstructural changes after aging at 650°C would falsify the proposed differential-Al-diffusion mechanism.
